root_cause.text: The lan966x FDMA driver had incomplete error cleanup in lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc() and lan966x_fdma_init(), failing to destroy the already-created rx->page_pool when later allocation steps failed, causing a page_pool resource leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds page_pool_destroy(rx->page_pool) when fdma_alloc_coherent() fails in lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(), and adds page_pool_destroy(lan966x->rx.page_pool) in lan966x_fdma_init() when lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc() fails after lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc() succeeded; the CVE/commit message explicitly says the page pool was created but “does not destroy it” in these error paths, “leaking the pool.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The lan966x FDMA driver had incomplete error cleanup in lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc() and lan966x_fdma_init(), failing to destroy the already-created rx->page_pool when later allocation steps failed, causing a page_pool resource leak.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds page_pool_destroy(rx->page_pool) when fdma_alloc_coherent() fails in lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(), and adds page_pool_destroy(lan966x->rx.page_pool) in lan966x_fdma_init() when lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc() fails after lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc() succeeded; the CVE/commit message explicitly says the page pool was created but “does not destroy it” in these error paths, “leaking the pool.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Destroy the allocated page pool when FDMA coherent allocation fails to avoid leaking resources on the error path.
intent_record.what: The change adds braces around the existing `if (err)` check after `fdma_alloc_coherent(lan966x->dev, fdma);` and inserts a call to `page_pool_destroy(rx->page_pool);` before returning the error.
intent_record.how: If coherent FDMA allocation fails, the function now releases the previously created page pool before exiting, preventing the page pool from being leaked on this error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Destroy the RX page pool when TX FDMA allocation fails so initialization cleanup does not leak resources.
intent_record.what: A call to page_pool_destroy(lan966x->rx.page_pool) was added in the error-handling branch of lan966x_fdma_init() when lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc(&lan966x->tx) fails, immediately after fdma_free_coherent(lan966x->dev, &lan966x->rx.fdma) and before returning the error.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if TX FDMA allocation fails during initialization, the RX page pool is now explicitly destroyed as part of cleanup, preventing the page pool resource from being left allocated on this failure path.

grouping_result.intent: Destroy the RX page pool when TX FDMA allocation fails so initialization cleanup does not leak resources.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure initialization error paths free the allocated RX page pool when subsequent FDMA buffer allocation fails to prevent resource leaks.

relevance_review.reason: The changes specifically add missing cleanup of the already-created RX page pool on later FDMA allocation failures in both rx_alloc/init error paths, directly addressing the page_pool leak described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: When fdma_alloc_coherent() fails after rx->page_pool has already been created, this immediate return exits without destroying rx->page_pool, directly causing the page_pool leak in lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc().

On lan966x_fdma_tx_alloc() failure during lan966x_fdma_init(), this return occurs after only freeing RX coherent memory; it does not destroy the already-allocated RX page pool, causing the initialization error-path leak.
This cleanup is incomplete: it frees RX coherent memory but omits destruction of lan966x->rx.page_pool before returning on error, embodying the faulty error handling that leaks the page pool.

vuln_statements.explanation: In lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(), this immediate error return is taken after rx->page_pool has already been created but before it is destroyed when a later coherent allocation fails, causing the leaked page_pool resource described in the root cause.

In lan966x_fdma_init(), this cleanup on TX allocation failure is incomplete because it frees only RX coherent memory and omits destruction of the already-created lan966x->rx.page_pool, directly contributing to the page_pool leak.
In lan966x_fdma_init(), this return exits the TX allocation failure path after incomplete cleanup, leaving the previously allocated RX page_pool undisposed and thus leaking the resource.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant error-handling logic is visible in the snippet, especially in `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()` and the setup in `lan966x_fdma_init()`, so the shown code is sufficient. In `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()`, the function first creates the page pool with `if (lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc_page_pool(rx)) return PTR_ERR(rx->page_pool);` and then immediately calls `err = fdma_alloc_coherent(lan966x->dev, fdma); if (err) return err;`. There is no cleanup of `rx->page_pool` on the later failure path after the page pool has already been created. Since this commit also wires RX allocation through callbacks in `lan966x_fdma_init()` via `lan966x->rx.fdma.ops.dataptr_cb = &lan966x_fdma_rx_dataptr_cb;`, later FDMA allocation/initialization can fail after `rx->page_pool` exists, but the function still just returns the error. This matches the root cause: incomplete error cleanup causing a leak of the already-created `rx->page_pool`. No fix is present here because there is no `page_pool_destroy(rx->page_pool)` (or equivalent cleanup) on the failure path in `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()`, and nothing in the shown `lan966x_fdma_init()` adds such cleanup either.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains both relevant functions, `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()` and `lan966x_fdma_init()`, along with the cleanup helpers they call. The vulnerable construct is present: in `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()`, after `rx->dcbs = dma_alloc_coherent(...)`, the nested allocation loop does `page = lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc_page(rx, db); if (!page) return -ENOMEM;`. This returns immediately on partial allocation failure without any cleanup of resources already allocated earlier in the function. Likewise, `lan966x_fdma_init()` does `err = lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(&lan966x->rx); if (err) return err;` and later, if TX allocation fails, it only calls `lan966x_fdma_rx_free(&lan966x->rx);` before returning. `lan966x_fdma_rx_free()` only frees the coherent DCB memory via `dma_free_coherent(...)` and does not free previously allocated RX pages (`lan966x_fdma_rx_free_pages()` is separate and not called here). Therefore, previously allocated RX page resources leak on these error paths. The fix is not present because there is no error unwinding in `lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc()` and no call sequence in `lan966x_fdma_init()` that frees RX pages on allocation failure; specifically, `lan966x_fdma_rx_free_pages(&lan966x->rx)` is only called in `lan966x_fdma_deinit()`, not in the init-time failure paths.
